decisions.reason: The quoted sentence directly states that 'Several small case series identified KCTD7 mutations in patients with a rare autosomal recessive disorder designated progressive myoclonic epilepsy (EPM3).' This directly establishes that KCTD7 mutations cause EPM3.

The quoted sentence directly states KCTD7 mutations are identified 'in patients with a rare autosomal recessive disorder designated progressive myoclonic epilepsy (EPM3) and neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (CLN14),' establishing causality for both disease forms.
The term 'progressive myoclonic epilepsy (EPM3)' explicitly includes myoclonus as a defining feature of the disease. EPM3 has myoclonus as a clinical phenotype.
The term 'progressive myoclonic epilepsy (EPM3)' explicitly includes epilepsy (seizures) as a defining feature. Seizures are a core phenotype of EPM3.

The term 'neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (CLN14)' defines the disease by the presence of lipofuscin accumulation. The abstract also confirms this by stating 'Biallelic KCTD7 mutations define a neurodegenerative disorder with lipofuscin and lipid droplet accumulation.' Lipofuscin accumulation is the defining phenotype of neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis.

The quote states 'KCTD7 deficiency appears to cause an underlying autophagy-lysosome defect conserved in yeast.' This establishes that KCTD7 deficiency has impaired autophagy as a mechanism. While the quote mentions the compound mechanism 'autophagy-lysosome defect,' impaired autophagy is clearly established as a mechanism caused by KCTD7 deficiency and is supported by the earlier statement about patient fibroblasts having 'impaired autophagy.'

The quote directly states 'KCTD7 deficiency appears to cause an underlying autophagy-lysosome defect conserved in yeast.' This explicitly establishes that KCTD7 deficiency has an autophagy-lysosome defect as a mechanism.

The quote states 'genetic analysis and impaired biochemical interactions with cullin 3 support a causal role for patient KCTD7 variants.' This indicates that KCTD7 has biochemical interactions with cullin 3, supporting the associated_with relationship.
